candidates.name: Czech Registr smluv (smlouvy.gov.cz): full-text contracts and attached supplier offers for Illumina and NovaSeq reagents at Czech universities and institutes, 2023–2026
candidates.access: This register is open and needs no login. Czech law requires public bodies to publish every contract over CZK 50K, with the PDF attached. Search the register for 'NovaSeq', 'Illumina' and 'SEQme' (a Czech Illumina distributor). Two example attachment URLs from search: https://smlouvy.gov.cz/smlouva/soubor/23051531/ (offer 'Nabídka, ÚMBR, SEQme') and https://smlouvy.gov.cz/smlouva/soubor/32253059/. For bulk work, use the monthly XML open-data dumps at https://data.smlouvy.gov.cz/ (that URL is from memory and was not opened) and filter predmet/text for NovaSeq. Pair this with TED 301608-2026 (Charles University 1st Faculty of Medicine, 'Kity pro sekvenování na přístroji NovaSeq X'). That framework is capped at CZK 12M, started 19 Feb 2024 and runs 2 years, so its call-off contracts and the successor 2026 framework should also appear in the register. Do not use the Hlídač státu API, because it needs a token.
candidates.rationale: This is the rare public source that publishes the actual signed offer, with unit prices per kit, not just a tender estimate. A repeat buyer such as Charles University or an Academy of Sciences institute buying 25B/10B kits under its 2024 framework and then its 2026 renewal gives a like-for-like net price per kit over time at flat quantities. That is exactly the 'research price down at flat volume' evidence 2B lacks. I confirmed by search that the register holds SEQme/Illumina offer PDFs; I did not open them.

candidates.name: TED repeat-buyer award series for Illumina consumables at research buyers (CPV 33696500 plus 'Illumina'), comparing each buyer's award value and quantities across years
candidates.access: Use the TED search API (POST https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search, no login). Query: FT~"Illumina" AND classification-cpv=33696500 AND notice-type in (can-standard, can-social), publication date from 20220101. Group results by buyer and keep only buyers with 2 or more awards. Confirmed 2026 seeds: Tartu Ülikool, 'Illumina genome sequencing consumables' awarded to Nova natura OÜ for €1,000,000, first published 24 Mar 2026 (bidsfactory mirror: https://bidsfactory.com/en/tenders/illumina-genoomiuuringute-aparatuuri-jooksevvahend-ted-85bd6b66f7807f66); Uniwersytet Medyczny w Łodzi, Illumina reagents by negotiated procedure without prior publication, 12 months from 1 Jun 2026 (TED 528143-2026 or 536530-2026 family); Charles University 301608-2026; Universität zu Köln 2023 award (TED 458387-2023 or 502315-2023). Pull each buyer's prior-cycle notice and compare value per year and lot quantities. This differs from S414 (clinical X replacements) and S474 (outsourcing awards).
candidates.rationale: Research institutes re-tender Illumina consumables every 1–2 years for roughly constant volumes, often directly with distributors because of patent exclusivity. If a buyer's annual award value falls while its kit quantities hold, that is research price erosion at flat volume. If awards come in below estimates, that is negotiated discounting. Some 2026 notices are only estimates, so look for 'final value' fields and lot-level quantities.

candidates.name: Slovak Central Register of Contracts (crz.gov.sk): full contract PDFs for NGS reagents and sequencer-plus-reagent frameworks
candidates.access: This register is open and needs no login. Search the full text for 'NovaSeq', 'Illumina' and 'sekvenátor'. Example attachments from search: https://www.crz.gov.sk//data/att/3093688.pdf, https://www.crz.gov.sk//data/att/2881306.pdf and https://www.crz.gov.sk//data/att/3027468.pdf. The last is the NÚDCH framework Z202119303_Z for a leased high-capacity sequencer plus reagents. Read the price annexes (cenová ponuka / príloha) for unit prices. If any PDFs are scanned images, they will need local text extraction.
candidates.rationale: Like the Czech register, this one publishes signed contracts with priced annexes. Slovak Medical University and the Academy of Sciences institutes buy Illumina kits repeatedly, so unit prices per kit can be compared across 2023–2026. The volume of hits is unknown, and the snippets I saw were mostly 2021 contracts.

candidates.name: Polish e-Zamówienia platform: bid-opening and award notices ('informacja z otwarcia ofert' / 'wybór oferty') giving offered prices for Illumina NovaSeq reagent lots at medical universities and institutes
candidates.access: The platform has a public search with no login. Search 'NovaSeq', 'Illumina odczynniki' and 'zestaw odczynników do sekwenatora', for 2023–2026. For each tender, open the 'Informacja z otwarcia ofert' attachment, which lists each bidder's gross price per lot, then the award notice. Seeds include UM Łódź (TED 2026 preannouncement), Instytut 'Pomnik-Centrum Zdrowia Dziecka' (AmpliSeq VEAT 2026; reagents awarded Dec 2024), Gdańsk, Warsaw and Wrocław medical universities, and PAN institutes. Many university procurement portals (platformazakupowa.pl/pn/<buyer>) mirror the same attachments publicly.
candidates.rationale: Polish law requires offered prices to be disclosed at bid opening, so repeat annual tenders for the same NovaSeq X kit list give a public price-per-kit series by buyer. It also shows whether Illumina distributors bid lower in 2026 than in 2024–25. I have not yet found NovaSeq-specific Polish hits beyond the TED preannouncements.

candidates.name: AGRF (Australian Genome Research Facility, the not-for-profit national provider): dated 25B lane promotions plus FY24-25 annual report revenue versus sample volume
candidates.access: Open the 2025 promotion page: 10% off a NovaSeq X 25B lane, 2–30 May 2025, 2.8–3.1B read pairs. Try sibling slugs for 2026 promotions (/25b-promo-2026, /promotions, the agrf-blog archive). Read the FY2024-25 annual report linked from https://www.agrf.org.au/store and AGRF's earlier blog posts on annual reports (https://www.agrf.org.au/agrf-blog/annualreport23). Also read Bioplatforms Australia's annual report (https://bioplatforms.com/annual-report-2025/) for any NCRIS-funded AGRF sample counts and revenue.
candidates.rationale: AGRF is a large national research service provider, not one of the US cores already swept. If AGRF's revenue is flat or falling while its sample or Gb counts are flat or rising, and promotions keep repeating, that shows research price per unit falling outside the US NIH story. Repeated promotions are a sign that discounting is becoming routine.

candidates.name: GENEWIZ/Azenta US 'claim promotions' page: NovaSeq X Plus data-package promotions for academics over time
candidates.access: The page is open. Current snippet: 375 Gb on NovaSeq X Plus for $1,450 (~$3.87/Gb), new academic customers only, no retroactive use. Capture the page now. Get the history from archive.ph (https://archive.ph/web.genewiz.com/*), not Wayback, because Wayback is blocked for WebFetch. Also probe sibling slugs on web.genewiz.com that Google indexes ('site:web.genewiz.com NovaSeq'). This is distinct from S351 (GENEWIZ Japan) and S428 (Azenta filings).
candidates.rationale: Azenta is a major US research outsourcing channel. A falling $/Gb on comparable 375 Gb or full-lane packages through 2025–26, set against its 'muted' multiomics volume, would show research price erosion passing through the outsourcing channel that already takes work from cores. The page is undated, so the archive history is essential.

candidates.name: WhatDoTheyKnow (UK FOI archive): published responses on university and NHS spend with Illumina Cambridge Ltd, sequencing consumables contracts and discount terms
candidates.access: The archive is public and needs no login for reading (do not file requests). Run searches for 'Illumina', 'NovaSeq', 'sequencing consumables' and 'genomics contract'. Download the attached response spreadsheets or PDFs, which often give annual spend by supplier for FY2022/23 to FY2025/26. If the site search is thin, use a Google 'site:whatdotheyknow.com Illumina' query.
candidates.rationale: FOI responses can give annual spend with Illumina by named universities or units. Spend that falls while sequencing activity is stable (cross-check with the department's reported output) points to price erosion. My one search showed no direct hit, so this is speculative.

candidates.name: Roche AXELIOS early-access and launch-stage academic pricing: Roche country ASHG pages and GenomeWeb launch coverage
candidates.access: Open the Roche Sweden ASHG 2026 event page and look for pricing, early-access program or academic-offer language. Then search GenomeWeb for free-access pages (https://www.genomeweb.com/node/654936 and /node/649916; skip anything paywalled). Also run searches for 'AXELIOS' with 'per sample', 'core facility' or 'rate' after ASHG (mid-Oct 2026) on .edu and .ac.uk domains. Roche said operational cost details would come later.
candidates.rationale: The first published academic AXELIOS service rates would let us compare price per sample directly with the 25B on the same core's rate sheet. That is the cleanest evidence that research price competition is reaching Illumina. Roche deferred operational cost details at launch (29 Jun 2026), so ASHG is the likely venue. Expected yield before ASHG is low.
